title: More stuff means a stronger gravitational tug
summary: Anything that has mass also has gravity, and a body with more mass tugs harder.
body: Space Place states two linked points in its December 2020 gravity article. First, mass and gravity go together: if a thing has mass, it has gravity. Second, a body that contains more mass produces more gravity than a body that contains less. A mountain therefore tugs more than a pebble, on that account. The page stops there. It does not write an equation.

sources.title: What Is Gravity?
sources.author: NASA Space Place
sources.note: NASA Space Place, article last updated 17 December 2020. Paraphrase of the page's own sentence. Public-domain US federal page. Supports 'anything that has mass also has gravity' and 'objects with more mass have more gravity'.
